description: Somos Cosmic Apus , un equipo apasionado por la ciencia y tecnología. Abordaremos el desafío de identificar ubicaciones terrestres análogas a bases en la Luna y Marte. Buscamos colaboradores en desarrollo , diseño multimedia y comunicación para proponer modelos de hábitats interplanetarios. ¡Únete al equipo!
summary: We developed the GeoAnalog AI platform, structured around three core interfaces: History, Data, and Mission Control. The first interface provides a historical and geomorphological overview of the Moon, incorporating previously cataloged sites derived from official NASA datasets. The second interface compiles a curated repository of validated geophysical and environmental parameters for both the Moon and Mars. Finally, the Mission Control interface enables interactive comparative simulations between lunar or Martian regions and their terrestrial analogs. Upon selecting any coordinate on the lunar surface, the system performs a rapid automated correlation against terrestrial locations, displaying percentage similarity indices, radiation levels, slope gradient, and a multivariable comparative chart evaluating five critical parameters: slope, surface roughness, albedo, temperature, and spectral signature. Additionally, the module integrates operational rover telemetry (including battery status and motor performance) alongside a risk-and-cost assessment simulation for lunar and Martian exploration missions.
details:
How it works:

  • The platform utilizes an optimized, lightweight JSON database (analogs.json) derived from NASA’s Earthdata topics (Land Surface, Solid Earth, Atmosphere, and Sun-Earth Interactions).
  • The interface dynamically renders an interactive world map highlighting key terrestrial analogs and running a fast comparison algorithm.
  • Live Demonstration: To showcase its real-time versatility, a physical hardware demonstrator named WALL-E navigates a simulated terrain, using onboard sensors to stream live telemetry to the platform, proving that the web application can instantly process and compare field data with NASA analogs.

Core Benefits:

  • Operational Efficiency: Overcomes the computational bottleneck of processing massive, raw satellite datasets (such as NetCDF or GeoTIFF files) in real-time by utilizing an optimized, lightweight data structure.
  • Seamless Telemetry Integration: Bridges geospatial scientific metrics with external live data sources effortlessly.
  • Scalable Rapid Prototyping: Provides a cost-effective, modular framework that can be easily replicated for field-testing planetary exploration technologies.

Anticipated Impact:

  • Optimized Analogue Selection: Equips researchers, students, and space exploration enthusiasts with an accessible, visual tool to identify optimal terrestrial environments for testing space hardware prior to actual missions.
  • Accessible Science Communication: Translates complex NASA Earth science data into an interactive, educational format suitable for academic evaluation and public outreach.

Technology Stack & Tools:

  • Software & Programming Languages (Core Platform):
  • HTML5, Tailwind CSS, & JavaScript: For frontend development of GeoAnalog AI
  • Leaflet.js: For interactive world map rendering
  • Chart.js: For real-time telemetry visualization
  • JSON (analogs.json): As a lightweight database for key analog sites
  • Python: For preliminary data structuring and variable filtering

  • Hardware & Mechatronics (WALL-E - Live Demonstrator):
  • ESP32 Microcontroller (Wi-Fi enabled)
  • Custom-designed articulated chassis with 4WD traction for rugged terrain mobility
  • Sensors: MPU6050 (IMU accelerometer/gyroscope), BME280 (temperature and humidity),BH1750 (ambient light/radiation simulation), and HC-SR04 (ultrasonic obstacle detection)

Project Creativity & Innovation:

The primary innovation of GeoAnalog AI lies in solving a complex engineering constraint—handling massive satellite data under strict time limitations—through an intelligent systems architecture. Rather than attempting heavy server-side processing, the platform establishes a harmonious bridge where live telemetry and NASA thematic data converge via a lightweight, real-time pipeline. Additionally, the integration of WALL-E demonstrates the platform's agility in connecting real-world physical simulations with spatial data analysis.

Key Design Considerations

  • Time Constraints (Hackathon Environment): Prioritized the delivery of a stable, functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) of the web platform over raw data overload by replacing heavy scripts with an optimized JSON framework.
  • Variable Parity: Ensured a strict logical correlation between physical sensor outputs from WALL-E and the four core scientific pillars (Rugosity, Soil Composition, Climate, and Radiation).
  • System Scalability:* Designed *GeoAnalog AI to be fully functional as a standalone web intelligence tool, with modular support for live telemetry inputs.
